_: Legends, redesigned (Ed, 2026-10-05; issue #87). What they are for (Ed, 2026-10-06): 'The idea of legends is that they provide a different layer of tasks to the tasks to the game, that are mostly optional. If you are quick and can do the quests you can get buffs from them; if you are lucky and find a relic they can be very powerful allies; and if you are losing, their babies get hurt during sieges and they get enraged (ideally this helps the loss spiral happen faster and more dramatically). I think you should be able to get the buffs at any time the legend is sleeping, not just before the soundsystem is made.' The rules: Asleep by default (soundsystems no longer wake them), dreaming of a creature (the quest): bring that creature's sigil into its area while its quest is open (as long as it sleeps, its area's soundsystem on or not: Ed, 2026-10-06; done before the area's wave, the area is friendly too and the ley line moves on) and you get its buff; it sleeps on. Restless while its area has none of its own kind (any state: wild, happy, leashed ones parked there, babies), its dream a nightmare (restlessness 0 to 1 over angryAfter seconds; checked every check seconds), calming back to sleep as soon as one of its kind is there again; at 1 it's angry. Happy once a relic is put down within placeRadius metres of it while it sleeps (or is restless): you get its buff, and it defends. Buffs, once earned, are never taken away. relics: count giant half-buried party objects per map (kinds from the art), in areas at least minRemoteness from home, at least spacing areas apart; walk up to one (within pickRadius metres) on the ground and press the sigil button: it's a relic sigil in your stack. attack (angry and happy alike; Ed 2026-10-05: long range, slow, less damage): a legend never leaves its area (it stands at home) but reaches range metres (about 2 to 3 areas); every interval seconds it winds up for windup seconds (telegraphed), then lobs (a bomb landing after lobFlight seconds, hitting everything within lobRadius) or beams (a line range long, beamWidth wide, burning for beamTime seconds), chosen per species (beam lists them); each volley hits up to targets of them (one lob or beam at each), damage a hit (the witch: one point, as ever); enraged animals within wornReach metres go for a happy one (it wears down); with nothing in reach it looks again every recheck seconds (balance, 2026-10-06: looking every step made 30 awake legends cost 17 times the rules). A happy one heals to whole over healTime seconds when nothing's near. (Balance builder's values, #80: legend damage is the game's most sensitive knob.) Angry: the witch and her posse only, never soundsystems or happy creatures. Happy: enraged ones only. Worn down (its health gone), a happy one goes back to sleep (its buff kept), an angry one too.
_charge: The long charge (Ed, 2026-10-05: "charging legends do long distance charges knocking away everything in the way... but they'd have to go back to their area after each one"; "medium speed (they're huge, and heavy), and they have a big slowdown arc afterwards. They can curve somewhat as they charge to hit their target"). species: the legends that charge instead of lobbing or beaming (those whose fight move is a charge). Every attack.interval seconds at home it picks its target as ever (attack.range), lowers its head for windup seconds (its first lane shown on the ground, laneShown metres of it), then runs: building speed at accel m/s a second to speed m/s (about her run), turning toward its target at up to turn degrees a second (a sharp sidestep or a blink beats it; drifting doesn't), until it's past its target or has run attack.range metres; then it brakes over brake metres, turning wide at arc degrees a second as it slows. Everything in its lane (laneWidth metres wide) but its own side and its own kind is hit once: damage, creatures knocked aside knockback metres (less as it slows); the witch loses her one point and is thrown aside and staggered as by any ram (tuning witch.knock: rules/knock.ts). It runs straight through scenery. Then it walks home at returnSpeed m/s to where it lay (rest seconds there before it may charge again): the trip home is its real cooldown. closeMoves: false (Ed, 2026-10-05: "stick with the long range one for now"): legends use only their long-range attack, near or far; true brings back their close-up move sets (slam, nova, charge; spin in phase 2) for wild legends.
